title: Tuned-Lens-Style Affine Alignment for Encoder Truncation in Whisper ASR: An Empirical Investigation

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to test whether tuned-lens-style representation alignment can make Whisper encoder truncation practical for speedup. No prior paper explicitly addresses this objective. While [3] ("Eliciting Latent Predictions from Transformers with the Tuned Lens") explores tuned-lens-style representation alignment, its focus is on understanding iterative inference in transformers rather than enabling encoder truncation for speedup. Similarly, [7] ("Training and Inference Efficiency of Encoder-Decoder Speech Models") and [13] ("Block Refinement Learning for Improving Early Exit in Autoregressive ASR") address efficiency improvements in encoder-decoder architectures but do not test representation alignment for truncation practicality. Thus, no prior paper shares the same purpose.

### Mechanism
The contribution's mechanism involves training affine and MLP translators to map truncated encoder states to the expected final-layer distribution across multiple depths. [3] ("Eliciting Latent Predictions from Transformers with the Tuned Lens") trains affine probes to decode hidden states into output distributions, which is substantively equivalent to the mechanism described here. Additionally, [6] ("Indic-TunedLens") applies affine transformations for interpretability in multilingual models, further confirming the mechanism's coverage. Both papers use the same primitive of mapping intermediate representations to output distributions, even if applied in different contexts.

### Evaluation
The evaluation systematically studies truncation depths on Whisper-large-v2, focusing on encoder latency reduction. [13] ("Block Refinement Learning for Improving Early Exit in Autoregressive ASR") conducts a systematic study of early exit techniques across intermediate layers in autoregressive ASR models, which is substantively equivalent in evaluation design. Both contributions evaluate layer-wise truncation strategies for computational efficiency, even though the specific benchmark (Whisper-large-v2) differs. Thus, the evaluation design is covered.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of Whisper encoder-decoder ASR and encoder truncation for speedup. [1] ("Simul-Whisper") and [7] ("Training and Inference Efficiency of Encoder-Decoder Speech Models") both address Whisper-based ASR and efficiency improvements, covering the same general application area. While [1] focuses on streaming ASR and [7] on training/inference efficiency, both papers operate within the Whisper encoder-decoder ASR domain, making the domain facet covered.
